topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the core learning outcomes regarding cancer etiology.

topics.label: Cancer etiology: intrinsic mutations, environmental risk, and epidemiological evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the genetic and evolutionary nature of cancer and explore how intrinsic errors, inherited traits, and environmental exposures contribute to cancer development.

topics.label: Infectious agents and viral mechanisms in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how infectious pathogens drive malignant transformation, focusing on Burkitt lymphoma as a prime example.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and metabolic activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which physical radiation and chemical agents cause DNA mutations directly or through xenobiotic metabolic activation.

topics.label: Tumor promoters, chronic inflammation, and tissue susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how non-mutagenic tumor promoters, chronic inflammation, and host developmental states drive neoplastic growth.

topics.label: Methodologies for evaluating carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the scientific methodologies used to identify carcinogens and assess their mutagenicity.

topics.label: Summary and risk-benefit considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a summary of environmental cancer risks and the daily balance of risks and benefits.
